name: Solar-Powered Grain Milling
summary: Photovoltaic-powered hammer mills and grain processing equipment that provide affordable and reliable milling services in off-grid and peri-urban communities.
description: Solar-powered grain milling systems use PV panels to power electric hammer mills, roller mills, and associated grain processing equipment. These systems replace diesel-powered mills, dramatically reducing operating costs and enabling communities in off-grid areas to access affordable milling services. In Uganda, solar milling units typically operate on 2–10 kW PV systems paired with batteries or direct DC-drive mills. Common configurations handle maize, sorghum, millet, cassava, and groundnuts. Solar mills are increasingly deployed as community enterprise facilities, operated by trained youth or women's groups as small agri-businesses. Some designs use direct solar DC drive systems with no battery, running only during daylight hours. Battery-buffered systems can work in the evening, improving utilisation. Solar milling can be standalone or integrated into broader solar energy hubs providing multiple services.
applications: Maize flour milling for household consumption and sale
Sorghum and millet milling in northern Uganda
benefits: Eliminates diesel fuel costs (major saving for operators)
Provides affordable milling in remote areas
Cleaner and quieter operation vs diesel mills
Can integrate with other solar applications (lighting, phone charging)
limitations: Limited milling output on heavily cloudy days (unless battery-backed)
Higher initial investment for battery-equipped systems
Electric mill components (brushes, bearings) require periodic servicing
Limited processing throughput compared to large commercial mills
Operator training needed for both solar system and mill
operationalNotes: Size PV array for expected daily milling workload (kg/day)
Include battery bank for 2–4 hours operation flexibility
Coordinate with local farmers on regular milling days to aggregate demand
Establish a community tariff schedule and payment system
Keep a maintenance log for all components
maintenanceNotes: Clean mill screen and hammers weekly
Replace hammer mill hammers every 3–6 months depending on usage
Lubricate bearings and drive shaft monthly
Clean PV panels weekly to maintain output
Inspect battery terminals quarterly and top up distilled water (flooded cells)
